rules.name: A retracement is a slower, shallower countertrend move that follows expansion without breaking the trend-defining swing
rules.setupAnchor: After a clear expansion, price pulls back against bias into an aligned area such as a fair value gap, order block, opening-price zone, or other higher-timeframe point of interest
rules.confirmationTrigger: Treat the move as a retracement while opposing candles overlap, displacement is reduced relative to the prior expansion, and the protected swing that validated the trend remains intact
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The protected swing created during the prior expansion is the structural line that the retracement should not violate
rules.invalidationCondition: Countertrend price accelerates like fresh expansion or closes through the protected swing that kept the original trend valid
rules.targetLogic: Primary expectation is resumption toward prior external liquidity or the next higher-timeframe objective once the pullback completes
exceptions: Not every expansion produces a tradable retracement
A fast opposite-direction displacement is more likely reversal than retracement
machineChecks: Require a prior expansion leg before retracement logic is enabled
Compare countertrend displacement and overlap against the prior expansion leg
Invalidate the retracement classification if the trend-defining protected swing is broken

rules.name: High-quality retracements pull into aligned points of interest and remain structurally shallow
rules.setupAnchor: Map the pullback into a fair value gap, order block, equilibrium-defined half, or other aligned point of interest inside the broader directional leg
rules.confirmationTrigger: Quality improves when price reaches the aligned area, shows failure-swing or sweep behavior, and continues to hold the correct side of the broader structure
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The prior protected swing defines the maximum acceptable depth while lower-timeframe structure can begin forming the next protected swing inside the retracement area
rules.invalidationCondition: The pullback trades too deep through the aligned area and protected swing, or reaches a higher-timeframe objective that implies the phase is changing
rules.targetLogic: Use the shallowest confirmed reaction area that still respects structure; deeper pullbacks reduce continuation quality
exceptions: Price does not need to touch an exact midpoint or exact candle open
Missing a retracement is preferable to forcing a late entry after price has already left the area
machineChecks: Track whether price has reached an aligned point of interest inside the active directional leg
Measure pullback depth relative to the prior expansion leg
Downgrade retracement quality when pullback depth reaches or breaks the protected swing

rules.name: A retracement completes when with-trend structure confirms again from the retracement area
rules.setupAnchor: After price reaches the retracement area, wait for a with-trend closure or protected swing to form from that area
rules.confirmationTrigger: A candle closes through the opposing candle series, or a new protected swing forms inside or just beyond the retracement zone in the trend direction
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The first new with-trend protected swing marks retracement completion and becomes the next invalidation level for the continuation entry
rules.invalidationCondition: Price revisits the zone without continuation confirmation, or breaks the newly formed protected swing immediately after entry
rules.targetLogic: Enter on confirmation or a validated retest and target external liquidity in the direction of the original trend
exceptions: Confirmation can occur on the structure timeframe or on a lower execution timeframe
Earlier lower-timeframe anticipation is riskier than waiting for higher-timeframe confirmation
machineChecks: Require a close through the opposing candle series or a new protected swing before continuation entry eligibility
Allow retest entries only after the with-trend confirmation exists
Store the new protected swing as the active invalidation level after retracement completion

rules.name: Skipped retracements and failed pullbacks should not be forced into entries
rules.setupAnchor: An expansion leg appears extended or price starts a shallow countertrend move that may become a pullback
rules.confirmationTrigger: Treat the move as tradable only when an aligned area, a valid reaction, and with-trend confirmation all appear together
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: If no new with-trend protected swing forms, the pullback remains unfinished or invalid as a continuation setup
rules.invalidationCondition: No valid area reaction occurs, no sweep or failure swing appears, or price transitions directly into consolidation or opposite expansion
rules.targetLogic: Stand aside and wait for either a later valid retracement or a different phase classification
exceptions: Strong expansions may skip retracements entirely
Once the higher-timeframe objective is met, expect a new phase instead of assuming another continuation
machineChecks: Block continuation entries when no aligned retracement area or confirmation exists
Block retracement classifications after the higher-timeframe objective has already been reached
Reclassify the move when opposite-direction expansion or range rotation becomes dominant
